rationale: Maintenance activity is a fair question for a GitHub-hosted skills collection, but nothing in the evidence addresses it. The GitHub items only describe what skills are, how to install them as a plugin marketplace, and availability on paid plans. None of them mention release cadence, changelogs, issue triage, or merged community pull requests. The only dated item (Dec 2025) announces the open standard, not repository activity.

The project ships every piece an agent needs to author a skill. There is a meta-skill, `skill-creator`, "for creating new skills and iteratively improving them", which can also benchmark them and optimize their descriptions. There is a `template/SKILL.md` and a formal Agent Skills spec covering the required frontmatter, description rules and directory layout. Packaging and distribution paths are documented through plugin manifests, `--plugin-dir` local testing, marketplaces and Skills API upload. Missing for 10: no hands-on or independent account of an agent completing the full author-to-package flow, and the evidence doesn't show `skill-creator` itself performing the packaging or upload step (only creation, improvement and benchmarking).

Skills are plain filesystem artifacts: dropping a `SKILL.md` into a skills directory is enough for Claude to add it to its toolkit, so an agent that can write files can install a skill without prompts. There is also a programmatic Skills API for uploads and a `--plugin-dir` flag for loading plugins. However, the documented marketplace path uses in-session `/plugin marketplace add` and `/plugin install` slash commands, and nothing explicitly describes a headless, promptless install an agent runs end to end. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented non-interactive install command or flag for agents, confirmation that plugin/marketplace install runs headlessly without prompts, and hands-on corroboration of agents self-installing skills.

Probes confirm a live llms.txt at code.claude.com/llms.txt and agent-fetchable Markdown versions of the docs pages (e.g. skills.md), each opening with a pointer to the full documentation index. Other docs, such as the platform skills guide and the agentskills.io specification, are also served as .md URLs, so an agent can be pointed straight at agent-oriented docs. Missing for 10: a Skills-specific llms.txt (the probed one covers Claude Code docs broadly), and independent hands-on corroboration that agents use these docs effectively.

Skills can package data-analysis workflows that Claude runs in a code execution environment. Anthropic says skills support "analyzing data using your organization's specific workflows", and ships pre-built skills such as xlsx and pdf, which a community user praised for handling Excel edge cases. However, the evidence never describes a built-in feature that surfaces AI-generated insights or suggestions from a user's data; that output depends on the user or Claude invoking a suitable skill. missing for 10: an explicit insight/suggestion capability over user data, documented examples of analysis outputs, independent hands-on corroboration of data-insight quality.

Skills run inside Claude, the built-in assistant. Users delegate tasks either by letting Claude load a relevant skill automatically or by invoking one directly with `/skill-name`. Bundled skills such as `/run` and `/verify` work without setup, and subagents and agent teams extend the ways work can be handed off. Several hands-on community reports say Claude often fails to pick up skills on its own and needs explicit triggering, though direct invocation still works. Missing for 10: reliable automatic delegation (community reports inconsistent auto-triggering), independent corroboration of end-to-end task delegation quality.

Skills can be used without any interactive UI. They are passed in the Messages API `container` parameter (up to 20 per request) and run in the code execution environment. They can be uploaded and managed through the Skills API, and controlled programmatically in Claude Agent SDK sessions, which docs describe as using Claude Code as a library for production agents. missing for 10: explicit CI/pipeline integration docs or examples (e.g., a GitHub Actions recipe or a non-interactive CLI mode for skills), and independent hands-on reports of headless or CI use.

Skills are a packaging format for Claude, not an MCP client themselves. The surrounding Claude Code plugin system, which distributes skills, can bundle MCP servers alongside skills, agents and hooks (docs-6, docs-21). The Claude Code host also connects to hundreds of external tools via MCP (docs-57). So MCP tool use comes through the companion host and plugin layer rather than the Skills format itself. Missing for 10: a native MCP-server declaration or wiring inside SKILL.md or the Agent Skills spec, MCP support on the Skills API/container path, detailed configuration docs, and independent hands-on corroboration.

Anthropic Skills is a skill-packaging standard and library, not an agent itself, so offering an official MCP server is a fair axis to judge. The evidence shows no such server. Plugins can bundle MCP servers and Claude Code can connect to MCP servers, but both are client-side or plugin-packaging features. Docs say Claude loads skills automatically when a natural-language request matches the skill's description, with `/skill-name` as an explicit fallback (docs-2, docs-25, docs-17, docs-32). Missing for 10: reliable natural-language triggering confirmed by independent hands-on evidence, and documentation of how natural-language routing behaves when it fails.
